document_title: The Every-day Life of Abraham Lincoln: A Narrative And Descriptive Biography With Pen-Pictures And Personal; Recollections By Those Who Knew Him
author: Francis F. Browne
claims: The United States forts and armaments on the Southern coast were delivered into the hands of the enemy, with the exception of Fort Sumter, which was gallantly held by Major Robert Anderson.
The Confederate attack upon Fort Sumter, a United States fort situated at the mouth of Charleston Harbor, South Carolina, on April 12, 1861, was the signal that civil war had actually begun.
Lincoln maintained a conciliatory policy toward the States in rebellion until their resort to arms and capture of forts and property of the United States decided the course of the administration.
Following the assault on Fort Sumter, Lincoln issued a proclamation asking for the immediate enlistment of 75,000 volunteers and summoned Congress to convene in an extra session on July 4th.
Lincoln considered withdrawing United States mails from seceded states if Fort Sumter was assaulted, believing the commencement of actual war justified it.
Following the fall of Fort Sumter on Sunday, April 14th, Stephen Douglas publicly stated his full support for the President in preserving the Union and defending the Federal capital.
Major Robert Anderson evacuated Fort Sumter in 1861.
Lincoln and Major Robert Anderson met again in 1861 after Anderson had evacuated Fort Sumter, during which Lincoln recalled Anderson mustering him into service in 1832.
